answer: Hypothesis: Original-study effect sizes exceed those of replications in ALL three domains (Social, Cognitive, Economics), not just one. Paired Fisher-z mean differences: Cognitive +0.289 [95% bootstrap CI 0.169–0.408], Social +0.233 [0.162–0.300], Economics +0.266 [0.114–0.439], with original > replication in 82–88% of pairs per domain (sign test p<0.01 all). The inflation is largest in effective replicability terms for Social (median relative_es 0.13, only 21% replications succeeded) vs Cognitive (0.65, 47%) and Economics (0.70, 61%), though raw inflation magnitudes do not differ significantly across domains (Mann-Whitney p>=0.27). Caveats: discipline is perfectly confounded with replication project, but the pattern holds in both projects (rpp +0.261, ee +0.266); excluding 18 sign-inverted pairs preserves conclusions (differences +0.18 to +0.22, all p<0.01); variance-weighted analysis weakens Economics evidence (+0.013, p=0.69), so original>replication inflation is best established for Social and Cognitive.

Paired Fisher-z differences: Cognitive +0.289 [0.169-0.408], Social +0.233 [0.162-0.300], Economics +0.266 [0.114-0.439]; original > replication in 82-88% of pairs per domain (sign test p<0.01). payload.workflow: Inspected 86-row merged dataset (no missingness in key effect-size/discipline/project columns; no duplicate pairs). Computed paired differences fiso-fisr and ro-rr per domain; 10,000-resample paired bootstrap 95% CIs; Wilcoxon signed-rank and sign tests; summaries of relative_es and replicated rates; disaggregation by replication project (rpp vs ee) to address discipline-project confounding; sensitivity analysis excluding 18 sign-inverted pairs; variance-weighted fixed-effect robustness check; cross-discipline Mann-Whitney comparisons.
